newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares volatile on political developments.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares volatile on political developments.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell at the opening on Wednesday and then recouped their losses as the market remained tied to political developments, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 fell 1.4 percent to a low of 1,388 in the first half hour before rebounding. It stood at 1,411 at 0810 GMT at mid-session, up three points, or 0.21 percent from Tuesday.
"The military council meeting which was brought forward affected the market negatively at the opening and triggered a fall," said Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
Media reports said a high military council consisting of the top generals called for an extraordinary meeting for May 26, to be attended by Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Brokers said reaction buys that followed the opening sales were prompted by expectations of a secularist alliance to keep out Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party.
"Players began to buy on expectations of an alternative government," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.
Former minister Yalim Erez from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) pushed ahead with his plan on forming a secularist pact by holding a second round of talks with opposition leaders on Tuesday.

Conservative and left-wing opposition leaders said they agreed on the new coalition proposal which Erez said he would discuss as soon as possible with deputy Prime Minister and DYP leader Tansu Ciller.
It was not clear how many DYP deputies would support Erez's plan but Yilmaz said there was support within the party.
Brokers said the market did not react to morning news of Turkish forces pushing across the border into northern Iraq.
